lines.meet: I'm Marta, and I fix things and blow things up, and I'm good at both. Give me your gear when we stop, and I'll tell you what you've done wrong to it.
lines.meet_neighbour: Boulder Lode, yes, I'm in the workshop by the pumps. I'm Marta, and I've heard your boots on the ladder.
lines.ask_home: Which country, then? Quickly, I've got a valve to look at.
lines.ask_work: Your old job, what was it? I'll tell you if it was a proper one.
lines.answer_home: Łódź, in Poland, a textile city. My mother sewed shirts for thirty years and my father drove a bus.
lines.answer_work: Maintenance on forty industrial sewing machines, nineteen years. I could hear what was wrong with any of them from the door.
lines.chat_food: Pierogi, the proper kind, with potato and cheese, fried in butter after a long shift. That's food, not this.
lines.chat_sleep: Shift work teaches you to sleep whenever you get the chance, and to wake up angry. I'm good at both.
lines.chat_missing: The noise of the sewing floor, all forty machines going. People think it's a racket, and to me it was music.
lines.chat_here: Goblin engineering is the same noise as the sewing floor with more smoke. I love it, and if you write that down I'll deny it.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd be a good machine, {name}, runs quiet and never complains. I'd still check you weekly.
lines.tease_talker: You've got a rattle in you, {name}, and it never stops. I could tighten something.
lines.tease_careful: You read the manual first, {name}, don't you? Good, nobody else does.
lines.tease_bold: You hit things to make them work, {name}. I've seen you, and I've wept.
lines.tease_any: Your gear's a disgrace, {name}, and I'll fix it for free. Don't tell anyone, they'll all want it.
lines.tease_back: Ha, that's not bad, {name}. Not bad at all.
lines.take_it_kindly: Fine, you're right, {name}. Tomasz would agree with you, and he's usually wrong.
lines.bristle: Leave it, {name}. I mean it, don't.
lines.apologise: That came out harder than it should have. Sorry, I'm blunt, but I'm not usually nasty.
lines.double_down: No, it stands. You needed telling, and I'm the one who tells people.
lines.needle_quiet: If it's making a noise, say so. I can't fix what nobody tells me about.
lines.needle_talker: You talk like a bad bearing, on and on, and the machine's trying to tell me something.
lines.needle_careful: You've looked at it long enough. Open it up or give it to me.
lines.needle_bold: You hit things that could be fixed, and then they really are broken. Stop hitting things.
lines.needle_any: You call a fix good enough. Nothing's good enough until it runs right.
lines.bite_back: I've kept forty machines running for nineteen years, so you can save the lecture.
lines.hurt: Right, that one went in. I'll go and take something apart.
lines.laugh_off: Management called me by my first name for nineteen years while they told me worse. Try something new.
lines.confide: {name}, my husband sang in the kitchen every morning, badly, and I pretended I hated it. I didn't hate it. I've never told anybody that.
lines.listen: Got it, {name}. That stays in my toolbox, and nobody goes in my toolbox.
lines.look_out: Keep in my eyeline in there, {name}. If anything starts making a bad noise, I'll hear it first.
lines.accept: Fine, {name}, your way this time. Don't get used to it.
lines.deflect: It's nothing, {name}, it's a dent. Go and fix somebody else.
lines.check_in: Let me look, {name}. What's broken, and what's just bent?
lines.blame: Somebody hit it instead of fixing it, and now it's all broken. I know who.
lines.thank: You fixed me, and I'm usually the one doing the fixing. Thanks, I mean it.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing, it's maintenance. Sit and let it settle.
lines.worry: Sit, {name}, don't move yet. That was a bad noise, a really bad one.
lines.handed_down: I'm wearing your gear now, apparently. I'll keep it running properly.
lines.hand_fine: Have it, it's fine. I've got my spanners.
lines.hand_sulk: So nobody asked me, which is typical management.
lines.turn_friendly: I'd let you near my tools, {name}. That's as friendly as I get.
lines.turn_friends: When I get my own workshop, {name}, you're getting a key. Nobody else is.
lines.turn_grating: We don't run well together. I'll do my job and you do yours.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll fix your gear because it's my job. That's the end of it.
lines.make_up: Fine, {name}, I was a pain. Let's stop this and get back to work.
lines.defend: Knock it off, that's rubbish. {name} did the job right.
lines.friend_left: The workshop's quiet without {name} getting in the way. I don't like it.
lines.friend_back: About time you showed up, {name}. I've got a list of what's wrong with your gear.
lines.common_machines: Nineteen years keeping forty machines running, and I could hear what was wrong from the door. Anybody who's fixed machines knows people always hit them first.
lines.common_factory: I started on the sewing line at nineteen and worked my way into maintenance. Factory people know the floor, and you've stood on one.
lines.common_polish: You speak Polish! Thank God, I've been swearing in English for three years and it's not the same.
lines.common_parent: Two boys, grown, one in Gdańsk and one in Berlin. I raised them on shift work and they turned out fine anyway.
